newsitem.title: MALTA: Valletta Investment Bank profit up.
newsitem.headline: Valletta Investment Bank profit up.

text.p: Valletta Investment Bank, the merchant banking subsidiary of Malta's Bank of Valletta group, made a pre-tax profit of 1.3 million Maltese pounds ($3.44 million) in the year up to September 30, 1996, group chairman John Grech said on Tuesday.

Grech told a news conference profit was up by 20 percent over the previous year. Non-interest income improved to 191,000 pounds in 1996 from 72,000 pounds in 1995 and earnings per share were up to 21.9 cents from 17.9 cents.

He said the money-broking service carried out in liaison with Bank of Valletta was now established as the core business of Valletta Investment Bank. During the past year the bank carried out reviews and analysed new proposals for bank lending amounting to 180 million pounds.

The bank has entered into an agreement with the Malta Development Corporation to act as financial intermediary for the European Community Investment Partners Scheme, which provides financial and other assistance for the setting up of joint verntures between ther European Union and Maltese companies.
